title: You be the judge: should my partner stop hogging my side of the bed?
content: My partner Dave and I are two stubborn boys who both adore a great night's sleep. But we cannot settle a disagreement about which side of the bed belongs to whom. We've recently moved into a new flat and the orientation of our room and bed has shifted. Now, the side of the bed I assumed was mine has become Dave's. We lived in our old flat for three and a half years. We slept like kings there: a humongous bed and individual duvets, which our Swedish friend had recommended for a good night's sleep. I was on the left side. I felt well rested and got into a great sleep routine. Due to the orientation of our new bedroom, Dave wants to be furthest from the door, so I'm now sleeping on the right side and he is on the left. He thinks the sides we sleep on should be interchangeable, depending on where the door is, but I say the left side is mine, no matter what. So I've been forced to sleep on what I deem to be the wrong side for the last few months. I find it challenging to fall asleep and can't get used to it. I'm a sensitive sleeper and it's a big thing to retrain yourself to sleep on a different side of the bed. I slept so well before. Now I'm tossing and turning, trying to sleep on a side of my body that feels unnatural. In the night, Dave and I move closer and closer to our old sides and bump into each other in the middle. My sleep is disturbed. I want to swap back. Dave views the sides of the bed as relative to where they sit in the room, and who wants to be closest to the door or window. He says Pádraig gets up at 4am for work, so if he's moving around the room, it's disruptive to his sleep. I like to stay on the side furthest from the door for this reason. Pádraig could learn to sleep on this new side, but I can't learn to sleep through his noise in the mornings. It's been suggested that we move the bed in our room. But if we moved the bed to suit him, it would be bad feng shui as the door would be too close to the bed. I believe there are other considerations around sleeping, beyond just: I like being on the left or right. Pádraig needs to adjust.
translation: 我的伴侣戴夫和我都是固执的人，都渴望睡个好觉。但我们无法就床的哪一边属于谁达成一致。我们最近搬进了新公寓，房间和床的朝向都变了，我本以为属于我的那半边床如今成了戴夫的。我们在旧公寓住了三年半，在那里睡得像个国王：一张大床加两条独立羽绒被，这是我们的瑞典朋友为睡个好觉推荐的。我睡在左边，感觉休息得很好，养成了良好的睡眠习惯。由于新卧室的朝向，戴夫想睡在离门最远的一边，所以我现在睡右边、他睡左边。他觉得睡哪一边应该视门的位置而定，可以互换，但我说左边就是我的，无论如何都是。于是过去几个月我被迫睡在我认为错误的一边，入睡困难，怎么也适应不了。我是个敏感的睡眠者，重新训练自己睡床的另一边是件大事。我之前睡得很好，现在却辗转反侧，试图睡在我觉得不自然的身体一侧。夜里，我和戴夫越来越靠近自己旧的位置，在床中央撞到一起。我的睡眠被打乱了。我想换回来。戴夫认为床的两边是相对于房间位置而言的，取决于谁想离门或窗最近。他说帕德里格早上4点就要起床上班，如果他在房间里走动，会影响他的睡眠，所以他想睡在离门最远的一边。帕德里格可以学会睡在新的一边，但我没法学会睡在他早上的噪音里。有人建议我们把床挪一挪，但那样的话门离床太近，风水不好。我觉得睡眠还有其他考量，不只是我喜欢左边还是右边，帕德里格需要适应。
summary: 情侣因搬家后床的朝向改变而争执睡哪一边：一方坚持绝对位置，另一方认为应随房间调整，请读者评判。

structure.summary: 帕德里格坚持左边属于自己，换了方向睡不好，想换回去
戴夫认为睡哪边应视门窗位置而定，自己需要远离门的安静
读者投票并给出建议：考虑作息、尊重旧习惯或挪床折中

hard.s: He thinks the sides we sleep on should be interchangeable, depending on where the door is, but I say the left side is mine, no matter what.
hard.t: 他觉得我们睡在哪一边应视门的位置而定、可以互换，但我说左边就是我的，无论如何都是。
hard.a: depending on 为现在分词作状语，意为取决于；no matter what 为让步状语，意为无论如何。

title: The only way is up: cycling Norway's mountainous Milky Way
content: Norway is a hilly country, shrugs Glenn Roar Berge. He's not wrong, though he is fond of an understatement. I'm in Valdres in southern Norway to explore the cycle routes that skirt the edges of Jotunheimen national park. For most of our three-day ride, we'll be following the Mjølkevegen, or Milky Way, a 155-mile route from Vinstra in the north to Gol in the south. It was developed after the second world war, when increased demand for fresh milk meant connecting the mountain farms with the towns below. While farming continues, the road has been embraced in recent years by gravel cyclists looking for a multi-day adventure far from towns and cities. Ruten Fjellstue is a traditional inn, set up for cross-country skiing in winter, hiking and biking in summer. My trip starts here and it's where I'll meet my guide and group, and pick up my hired bike. These small inns are part of what makes cycling through the region work. At breakfast, there's an expectation that you'll make your own sandwiches from the buffet. Cycling here is powered by sandwiches, waffles with sour cream and berry jam, and plenty of cinnamon buns. Our first morning begins with a cruisy downhill run before the road turns into a rough track. A temporary road closure has sent us on to a mountainous diversion. I've never used drop handlebars before and it takes me a while to figure out the gears. While you don't have to be a typical Norwegian to enjoy these trails, a certain tolerance for hills helps. As we descend towards Lake Vinstre, the Jotunheimen mountains appear ahead. The lake is a deep turquoise-blue, and the shores are dotted with tiny wooden farmhouses painted red or yellow, many with grass roofs for extra protection when the snow arrives. We're cycling for long days, averaging about 45 miles a day, with 1,500 metres ascent, but there are gentler ways to experience the route: shorter stages mean more time to explore the cosy family hotels. I decide to lean in to taking it slowly, drinking in the spaciousness and letting the miles roll by. On my last day, the weather turns. We reach the bottom of a mountain pass in driving rain. There's a small cafe here, so we stop for waffles. Then the only way is up, and up, and up. It's 600 metres of elevation in just 6km. At the top, it's flat and exposed, and the clouds have transformed the mountains again. In this part of Norway, hotels are never built at the bottom of the valley. For a cyclist, this means that every day there is a final few kilometres up to the hotel. It's tough, but it makes the arrival all the sweeter. And the best views are those you've earned.
translation: 挪威是个多山的国家，格伦·罗尔·贝格耸耸肩说。他说得没错，虽然他喜欢轻描淡写。我来到挪威南部的瓦尔雷斯，探索环绕尤通黑门国家公园边缘的骑行路线。三天的大部分行程，我们沿着被称为银河之路的250公里路线骑行，它从北部的温斯特拉到南部的高尔。这条路建于二战后，当时鲜奶需求增加，需要把山间农场与山下城镇连接起来。如今务农仍在继续，但这条路近年来深受砾石自行车爱好者的青睐，他们寻找远离城镇的多日冒险之旅。鲁滕客栈是一家传统客栈，冬季提供越野滑雪、夏季提供徒步和骑行。我的旅程从这里开始，我将在此与向导和团队会合，领取租来的自行车。这些小店正是骑行穿越该地区可行的重要原因。早餐时，你会被期待用自助餐自己动手做三明治。在这里骑行靠三明治、酸奶油浆果酱华夫饼和大量肉桂面包提供能量。第一天早晨，我们先是一段轻松的 downhill 下滑，随后道路变成崎岖的土路。我从未用过弯把，花了好一会儿才弄明白变速。享受这些路线不需要成为典型的挪威人，但一定的爬坡耐受力很有帮助。我们的长骑平均每天45英里，爬升1500米，但也有更轻松的方式：更短的行程意味着更多时间探索温馨的家庭旅馆。我决定放慢节奏，尽情享受辽阔，让里程在脚下延伸。最后一天天气变了，我们在瓢泼大雨中抵达山口底部。这里有个小咖啡馆，我们停下来吃华夫饼，然后就是一路向上、向上、再向上——6公里爬升600米。到了顶上，地势平坦开阔，云层又改变了群山的面貌。在挪威这片地区，旅馆从不建在山谷底部，对骑行者来说，这意味着每天最后都有几公里爬坡才能到旅馆。这很艰难，但让抵达的喜悦更加甜美。最美的风景，总是你辛苦挣来的。
summary: 作者骑行挪威银河之路，穿越高山湖泊与传统客栈，体验爬坡的艰辛与挪威山地风光的壮美。

structure.summary: 沿二战后修建的送奶之路骑行，入驻传统客栈
长日爬坡、湖光山色、羊群惊险与挪威式补给
天气骤变中的最后爬坡，最美的风景是挣来的

hard.s: While you don't have to be a typical Norwegian to enjoy these trails, a certain tolerance for hills helps.
hard.t: 享受这些路线不需要成为典型的挪威人，但一定的爬坡耐受力很有帮助。
hard.a: while 引导让步状语从句；a tolerance for 意为对…的耐受；helps 为省略主语的强调（指爬坡耐力有帮助）。

title: Açaí, chipotle and gnocchi – words you are probably mispronouncing
content: The English language can seem designed to trip us up, whether we're greeting a colonel or travelling to Worcestershire. Açaí is the most mispronounced word in the UK, often rendered in speech as ack-eye or ah-sigh. How should I be saying it? Ah-sigh-ee. Açaí is just the tip of the iceberg. It tops a new list of 20 commonly mispronounced words. Quinoa came fourth; gnocchi came fifth; chipotle was seventh. Not all the words on the list are foods. Segue, often mispronounced seeg instead of segway, was second. Worcestershire came sixth. The list is from a recent poll of 2,000 people commissioned by Škoda, the Czech car company. Why would a Czech car company care how I pronounce chipotle? I think it is trying to make a point because Škoda is often mispronounced as scoder rather than shkoda. And, obviously, it's a publicity thing. Beneath the confusion over imported foodstuffs and the never-ending debate about how to say gif, it does seem that an identity crisis is unfolding. People in Britain have forgotten that some of their peculiar pronunciations make English a nightmare for foreigners. The word colonel came 15th in the poll. Some British people think it's pronounced as it is spelt, when it should be pronounced kernel, which isn't how it is spelt. Likewise, some of those polled mistakenly pronounced squirrel as a single-syllable word to rhyme with girl, instead of a two-syllable word. It's pronounced chi-poht-lay. Açaí first came to western countries from South America as freeze-dried pulp in the 1990s. It is a small, dark-purple berry, or a purée made from them, commonly used in smoothies. Those accents on the letters are designed to help you pronounce the word correctly. They're no help to me, but the poll shows millions of people share my confusion.
translation: 英语这门语言似乎专为绊倒我们而设计，无论是向陆军上校打招呼还是去伍斯特郡旅行。Açaí（巴西莓）是英国最容易读错的词，常被念成艾克艾或阿塞。该怎么读？阿塞伊。Açaí 只是冰山一角，它高居一份20个常见读错词榜单之首。藜麦排第四，意面疙瘩排第五，墨西哥辣椒酱排第七。榜单上并非都是食物：Segue（过渡）常被误读为西格而不是塞格威，排第二；伍斯特郡排第六。这份榜单来自最近一项对2000人的调查，由捷克汽车公司斯柯达委托进行。捷克汽车公司为什么关心你怎么读墨西哥辣椒酱？我想它想借此说明一点：斯柯达常被误读为斯科达而非斯柯达。当然，这也是公关噱头。在对外来食品的困惑和关于 gif 怎么说的无休止争论之下，似乎正上演一场身份危机。英国人已经忘记，他们某些古怪的发音让英语对外国人来说是一场噩梦。colone（上校）一词在调查中排第15。一些英国人以为它按拼写读，而它应读作 kernel（内核），这跟拼写毫无关系。同样，一些人误把 squirrel（松鼠）读成与 girl 押韵的单音节词，而它其实是一个不与任何词押韵的双音节词。它读作奇波特勒。巴西莓在20世纪90年代以冻干果浆的形式首次从南美传入西方国家。它是一种深紫色小浆果，或由其制成的果泥，常用于思慕雪。字母上的重音符号正是为了帮你正确发音。它们对我毫无帮助，但调查显示，数百万人和我一样困惑。
summary: 英国一项调查列出20个最常读错的英文词，从巴西莓到上校，揭示英语发音的混乱与身份焦虑。

structure.summary: 巴西莓居首，藜麦、意面疙瘩等食物词频繁上榜
斯柯达委托调查，借机调侃自家品牌常被读错
英国人的特殊发音让英语对外国人如噩梦，折射身份危机

hard.s: Beneath the confusion over imported foodstuffs and the never-ending debate about how to say gif, it does seem that an identity crisis is unfolding.
hard.t: 在对外来食品的困惑和关于 gif 怎么说的无休止争论之下，似乎正上演一场身份危机。
hard.a: beneath 意为在…之下；it does seem 为强调结构；identity crisis 意为身份危机。

title: 20 mortifying money conversations with friends – and how to handle them
content: Summer is the season of socialising, from alfresco drinks to weddings to group holidays. It can get expensive – and suddenly you start noticing those friends who don't pay their way. Or the ones who splash the cash and make you feel cheap. In fact, there are a host of annoying money-related habits that can cause tension among friends. British pub etiquette seems simple: in a group of friends, everyone takes it in turns to buy the drinks. In practice, it is a minefield. There's always someone who hangs back in the hope it won't come round to them; someone who orders half a lager when it's their turn to pay and a double G&T when it's yours; couples who see themselves as one entity when it comes to paying, but not when it comes to drinking. Ellie Austin-Williams, the London-based author of Money Talks, says it is best to bring it up straight away. Have the conversation at the start: do you want to do a round, or shall we pay our own way? People feel it's too awkward, but it's better to say: I'll buy my own, I'm not drinking today. People really do respect that. Conversely, if you've all agreed upfront to do rounds, it's harder for someone to shirk their turn. Matt Altmix, who is based in Atlanta and co-hosts the podcast How to Money, suggests budgeting for pub trips. If you're happy with how much you've decided to spend that night, you don't need to obsess about what everyone else is doing. That way, you're actually having a good time. Warning: this may mean going to the pub less often. Skipping out sometimes is totally acceptable. Then when you do show up, make it count. Alex Holder, the author of Open Up, rejects round culture altogether. It's presuming we're all going to drink the same amount. Not everyone wants to drink five drinks. Rather than noticing that someone gets a cheap drink when they're paying and feeling enraged, exit the culture.
translation: 夏天是社交的季节，从户外小酌到婚礼再到团体度假。这可能会很花钱——你突然开始注意到那些不付自己那份的朋友，或者那些大手大脚花钱、让你觉得自己寒酸的人。事实上，有一大堆令人恼火的金钱习惯会在朋友间引发紧张。英国酒吧的规矩似乎很简单：一群朋友中，大家轮流买酒。但实际上这是一个雷区。总有那么一个人故意往后缩，指望轮不到自己；轮到某人付钱时只点半杯拉格，轮到你时却点双份金汤力；有些情侣付钱时把自己看作一个整体，喝酒时却不这么算。伦敦作家埃莉·奥斯汀-威廉姆斯说，最好直截了当提出来：一开始就说清楚，你们要轮流买，还是各付各的？人们觉得这很尴尬，但最好说：我自己付，我今天不喝酒。人们真的会尊重这一点。反过来，如果大家一开始就约定轮流买，某人想逃避自己的回合就难了。亚特兰大的播客主持人马特·奥特米克斯建议为酒吧聚会做预算。如果你对自己当晚决定花的钱感到满意，就不必纠结别人在做什么。那样你才能真正玩得开心。警告：这可能意味着少去酒吧。偶尔跳过完全可以接受，等你去的时候，就让它值得。作家亚历克斯·霍尔德干脆反对轮流买酒文化：那是假定我们都喝同样的量，不是每个人都想喝五杯。与其注意到某人付钱时点便宜酒而愤愤不平，不如退出这种文化。
summary: 朋友间的金钱习惯（轮流买酒、AA制）常引发尴尬与紧张，专家建议开场就讲清楚、做预算或干脆退出。

structure.summary: 轮流买酒文化成为雷区，总有人逃避或占便宜
一开始就约定各付各的，或为社交做预算
反对者建议彻底退出轮流买酒文化

hard.s: There's always someone who hangs back in the hope it won't come round to them; someone who orders half a lager when it's their turn to pay and a double G&T when it's yours.
hard.t: 总有那么一个人故意往后缩，指望轮不到自己；轮到某人付钱时只点半杯拉格，轮到你时却点双份金汤力。
hard.a: 分号连接两个并列分句；hang back 意为退缩；in the hope 意为怀着…的希望；come round to 意为轮到。

title: Frugal or foolish? Manchester United may regret not backing Carrick
content: Another left-back has been a priority all summer, but there seems to be no sign of one coming to Old Trafford. After signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka in 2019, Manchester United's PR machine boasted they had scouted 804 right-backs before landing on the Crystal Palace player. Now, as the search for a left-back to challenge Luke Shaw drags on with less than two weeks of the summer transfer window remaining, there seems to be a lack of credible targets. United's analysts this summer plumped for a prodigious English full-back playing for one of the Premier League middleweights. That player, Lewis Hall, ticks many boxes for the club except for the price, with Newcastle slapping a premium on the 21-year-old. United have indicated a reluctance to pay over the odds for players and hence negotiations for Hall have hit the rocks. However, United's need for a left-back reinforcement to help out Shaw is clear. The 31-year-old started every Premier League game last season and performed solidly, but his history with injuries is such that another ever-present campaign is highly unlikely. With the return of Champions League football, United should play upwards of 50 games. That leaves one major area of concern, heightened by the fact Shaw struggled in a pre-season defeat on Saturday. United will be fairly happy with their midfield business if and when they get a deal for Carlos Baleba done. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have impressed in pre-season. A third new midfielder was always needed to reduce the burden on Santos, Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo over a long season. We've done really good business, Carrick said last week. We're delighted with that but we want more, we need more. But if Carrick is to push for one final marquee signing, can United afford not to fully back their manager when there is a hole in the squad? Sir Jim Ratcliffe has gained a reputation for penny-pinching since acquiring a minority stake in the club. His drive to save money has been controversial. Many believe refusing to spend more would equate to hanging a bright young manager out to dry. Having won 12 of his 17 matches in charge, most agree Carrick has earned the right to lead United for a full campaign. Failing to sign another left-back could be a costly transfer mistake from the Old Trafford hierarchy.
translation: 整个夏天，补强左后卫都是优先事项，但似乎没有迹象表明有球员会来到老特拉福德。2019年签下万比萨卡后，曼联的公关机器曾吹嘘他们考察了804名右后卫。如今，在夏窗仅剩不到两周之际，寻找一名挑战卢克·肖的左后卫仍在拖延，似乎缺乏可信的目标。曼联分析师今夏相中了一名效力于英超中游球队的出色英格兰边后卫。这名球员是刘易斯·霍尔，除了价格，他各方面都符合俱乐部的需求，纽卡斯尔对这位21岁小将标出了溢价。曼联表示不愿为球员支付过高价格，因此霍尔的谈判已陷入僵局。然而，曼联补强左后卫、为肖分担压力的需求十分明确。31岁的肖上赛季首发全部联赛，表现稳健，但他的伤病史意味着再次全勤几乎不可能。随着欧冠回归，曼联应踢50场以上比赛。这留下了一个主要隐患，周六季前赛失利中肖的挣扎更加剧了这一点。如果卡里克要推动最后一笔重磅签约，在阵容存在缺口时，曼联能不支持自己的主帅吗？拉特克利夫爵士自入股以来以吝啬闻名，他省钱的做法一直备受争议。许多人认为拒绝再多花钱等于把一位才华横溢的年轻主帅架在火上烤。执教17场赢下12场，大多数人认为卡里克赢得了带队打完整赛季的权利。若未能再签一名左后卫，可能是老特拉福德高层一个代价高昂的转会失误。
summary: 曼联迟迟未签左后卫补强，财政谨慎引发争议；主帅卡里克带队成绩出色，缺人恐成代价高昂的转会失误。

structure.summary: 左后卫目标霍尔因价格谈崩，阵容缺口明显
卡里克想再要重磅引援，中场已补强到位
老板吝啬受质疑；不签左后卫恐成转会失误

hard.s: Having won 12 of his 17 matches in charge, most agree Carrick has earned the right to lead United for a full campaign.
hard.t: 执教17场赢下12场，大多数人认为卡里克赢得了带队打完整赛季的权利。

title: Instant classics, odd inspirations and barcodes: 2026-27's best and worst kits
content: The Premier League season kicks off on Friday and masses of fans will be pulling on their teams' shiny new strips. There were some lovely efforts at the World Cup, and others more tedious than a 0-0 draw. It's a mixed bag once again. Manchester City have gone with an ombre design, which feels exhausted as a look in 2026. In the most surprising but successful collaboration, Sunderland have teamed up with Elvis Presley, or his estate, anyway, for a pink away shirt that nods to the supporters' anthem Can't Help Falling in Love. Chelsea's new home kit may look like the sort of thing a team would wear in an early video game, but it is pretty neat. I cannot stress this enough: the lack of a corporate logo will always make a shirt look better. The 90s polo-shirt collar is a popular aesthetic this season. Liverpool has surely produced the kit of the season. An entirely unsubtle homage to the 1989-91 home jersey, the home shirt is a blast of fun at a time when football is increasingly dispiriting. The white away kit is also a handsome affair, proving that white strips do not have to be boring. Hull's kit feels like it belongs on a glorious swamp of a pitch in the mid-to-late 20th century. The official reference point is the Tigers' late 70s aesthetic: wide black and amber stripes and a white collar and trim. It is definitely understated, given how many riotous designs the club has had in the past. It is extremely low-hanging fruit to compare Newcastle's shirt to a barcode, but, seriously, look at it. It's a barcode. It's also dizzying to the eye. The away strip is an improvement; a refined navy, it has a nice alternative badge of the city's castle. Ipswich secure the trophy for the most eye-rolling kit inspiration. The motif on the round-necked, blue home shirt is, according to the press release, a tribute to the stadium's floodlights. Manchester United's red home shirt has thick white stripes, while the white shorts have black stripes. This looks like one half each of two separate kits. The shirt itself is beautiful; the perfect shade of red, a retro collar, but the black touches are not strong enough to cohere with the massive stripes on the shorts.
translation: 英超联赛周五开赛，大批球迷将穿上球队闪亮的新球衣。世界杯上有些不错的作品，也有一些比0-0平局还乏味的。又一次喜忧参半。曼城采用了渐变色设计，在2026年看来这种样式已经审美疲劳。在自奥利维亚·罗德里戈与罗伯特·史密斯合作以来最出人意料却又成功的合作中，桑德兰与猫王埃尔维斯·普雷斯利（或其遗产方）联手推出粉色客场球衣，致敬球迷长久以来的非官方队歌《无法不爱上》。切尔西的新主场球衣看起来像早期电子游戏里叫伦敦蓝的球队会穿的那种，但相当利落。我要强调：没有赞助商标识，球衣永远更好看。90年代polo领是本赛季流行的美学。利物浦无疑拿出了赛季最佳球衣，完全不加掩饰地致敬1989-91年主场球衣，在足球日益令人沮丧的时代带来一阵欢乐。白色客场球衣也很漂亮，证明白色条纹不必乏味。赫尔城的球衣感觉属于20世纪中后期一片辉煌的泥泞球场，官方参照是老虎队70年代末的美学：宽大的黑琥珀条纹配白色衣领和镶边。把纽卡斯尔的球衣比作条形码是件太容易的事，但说真的，你看看它。那就是条形码，还让人眼晕。客场球衣则有所改进，精致的海军蓝，配以城市城堡的别致徽章。伊普斯维奇获得最令人翻白眼的球衣灵感奖：圆领蓝色主场球衣上的图案，据新闻稿称，是向球场灯光致敬。曼联的红色主场球衣配粗白条纹，白色短裤却配黑条纹，看起来像两套球衣各取一半。球衣本身很漂亮，完美的红色调，复古领口，但黑色点缀不足以与短裤上粗大的条纹协调。
summary: 新赛季英超球衣盘点：利物浦复古致敬、切尔西无赞助简洁亮眼，纽卡条形码、曼联双色条纹遭吐槽。

title: Patients in Yorkshire complain AI GP receptionist cannot understand accent
content: Patients in a South Yorkshire town are frustrated by AI GP receptionists not understanding their broad accents, a health watchdog has said. Healthwatch Rotherham said a number of practices in the area had introduced a new AI receptionist called Emma. It said it was hearing accounts of the AI not understanding local accents. Its manager told the BBC: 'One of the issues is this system can't always understand what people's inquiry is about due to their broad Yorkshire accent. Across South Yorkshire, accents do vary quite a lot. There are different twangs so there's a lot of variation. It seems the system isn't always able to understand, so that causes frustration.' The system, which is being used by an increasing number of GP surgeries across the UK, aims to answer every patient call instantly, eliminating the often long wait times patients experience in a phone queue. The manager said Emma had the potential to be a good system, but one disgruntled patient told Healthwatch: 'I could never get it to understand me, I ended up just hanging up and not bothering to try and book an appointment.' The feedback came after the watchdog reached out to groups representing older people and veterans communities. Some of the people were so frustrated at not being able to understand how to navigate this AI system, it was forcing them to travel back to their GP surgery in person. The usual route of using a telephone was no longer a comfortable process for them. Healthwatch said concerns around Emma were heightened when considering people less confident about using digital technology, or people with disabilities. It's important to remember that GP practices still have a legal duty to make reasonable adjustments for patients who need them. If using an AI receptionist is difficult for you, you can ask your practice what alternative ways are available to access services. QuantumLoopAI, the company behind the Emma system, said it was designed to understand a range of dialects and patients could speak to a human at any time. Emma does not make clinical decisions. Where she is unable to understand or deal with a patient's request the call is transferred to the reception team. No caller is required to continue speaking with Emma.
translation: 南约克郡一个小镇的病人对 AI 全科医生前台听不懂他们浓重的口音感到恼火，一家健康监督机构如此表示。罗瑟勒姆健康观察组织称，当地多家诊所引入了一种名为 Emma 的新 AI 前台。该组织表示听到一些 AI 听不懂当地口音的反映。其负责人告诉 BBC：问题之一是，由于他们浓重的约克郡口音，这个系统并不总能听懂人们的询问是什么。整个南约克郡的口音差异很大，有不同的腔调，变化很多。看来系统并不总能听懂，这造成了挫败感。这一系统正被英国越来越多的全科诊所使用，旨在即时接听每个患者来电，消除患者排队等前台接听的长久等待。该负责人说 Emma 有潜力成为一个好系统，但一位不满的患者告诉她：我从没能让它听懂我，最后只好挂断电话，不再费劲预约。这些反馈是该监督机构联络代表老年人和退伍军人社区的组织后获得的。有些人因无法弄明白如何操作这套 AI 系统而极度沮丧，被迫亲自跑回诊所。过去常用的电话途径对他们来说已不再舒适。健康观察组织表示，在考虑对数字技术不太自信的人或残障人士时，对 Emma 的担忧更为突出。重要的是要记住，诊所仍有法律义务为需要的患者做出合理调整。如果使用 AI 前台对你有困难，可以询问诊所有哪些替代途径获得服务。Emma 系统背后的公司表示，它被设计用来理解多种方言，患者随时可以与人通话。Emma 不做临床决定。当她无法理解或处理患者的请求时，电话会转给前台团队。没有任何来电者被要求必须继续与 Emma 交谈。
summary: 英国诊所引入 AI 前台 Emma，却因听不懂约克郡口音让患者受挫，老年人被迫亲自跑诊所，引发数字鸿沟担忧。

老年人和残障人士受挫最深，被迫亲自前往诊所
Emma 支持17种语言，无法理解时可转人工，随时可要求与工作人员通话

hard.t: 有些人因无法弄明白如何操作这套 AI 系统而极度沮丧，被迫亲自跑回诊所。
hard.a: so...that 结构（that 省略）；frustrated at 意为对…感到沮丧；navigate 此处意为操作、应对；in person 意为亲自。

title: Young vapers at risk of breathing problems and becoming smokers
content: Young people who start vaping risk developing breathing problems and going on to smoke cigarettes, children's doctors have warned. Child vaping is consistently linked with poor respiratory health, such as coughing, wheezing, bronchitis symptoms and asthma exacerbations, while vapes have been shown to act as a gateway to smoking cigarettes, according to one of the most comprehensive reviews of the available evidence undertaken by the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health. The review's co-author, Prof Will Carroll, said: 'Vaping should not be seen as a harmless part of growing up. The evidence shows clear links with respiratory symptoms, nicotine dependence and subsequent cigarette smoking, while concerns about wider impacts on young people's health continue to grow.' He urged the government to quickly implement the new measures announced in July, which include plain packaging, moving vapes out of sight in shops, and restrictions on vape flavour names to move away from names inspired by sweets, desserts and alcohol in favour of simpler names such as apple. Carroll also called on the government to go further, including by limiting the number of flavours available. Vaping has surged in popularity over the past decade, with rates of experimentation and regular use among young people increasing about tenfold, and use often beginning in adolescence. An estimated one in five of 11-17-year-olds in Britain have tried vaping. The review also identified evidence linking vaping to poor oral and dental health, and negative mental health outcomes, such as anxiety, depression and suicidal ideation. The vice-president for policy at the Royal College said that as vaping was a relatively new product, there is much we do not yet know about its long-term impact. But a clear and concerning picture is emerging. The new law is an important step towards protecting children from nicotine addiction, but it must not be seen as a one-and-done solution. We need to keep pace with a rapidly evolving market and continue to take action to protect children from nicotine products that are deliberately made and marketed to appeal to them.
translation: 儿童医生警告，开始吸电子烟的年轻人有患上呼吸问题并继而吸香烟的风险。英国皇家儿科与儿童健康学院开展的最全面证据评估之一显示，儿童吸电子烟始终与呼吸道健康状况不佳相关，如咳嗽、喘息、支气管炎症状和哮喘加重，同时电子烟已被证明是吸香烟的入门通道。该评估的共同作者威尔·卡罗尔教授说：电子烟不应被视为成长过程中无害的一部分。证据显示其与呼吸道症状、尼古丁依赖及随后的吸烟存在明确联系，而人们对电子烟影响年轻人健康的更广泛担忧也在增长。他敦促政府迅速落实7月宣布的新措施，包括素色包装、将电子烟移出商店视线，以及限制电子烟口味名称——摆脱受糖果、甜点和酒类启发的名字，改用苹果等更简单的名字。卡罗尔还呼吁政府更进一步，包括限制可用口味的数量。过去十年电子烟人气激增，年轻人的尝试率和常规使用率增长约十倍，且使用往往始于青春期。据估计，英国11至17岁青少年中约五分之一尝试过电子烟。该评估还发现了电子烟与口腔和牙齿健康不佳（包括炎症、溃疡和口干）以及负面心理健康结果（如焦虑、抑郁和自杀意念）相关的证据。皇家学院的政策副总裁表示，由于电子烟相对较新，对其长期影响还有很多未知，但一幅清晰而令人担忧的画面正在浮现。新法律是保护儿童免于尼古丁成瘾的重要一步，但不能被视为一次性解决方案。我们需要跟上快速演变的市场，继续采取行动，保护儿童免受那些刻意制造和营销以吸引他们的尼古丁产品的侵害。
summary: 综合评估显示青少年吸电子烟与呼吸问题、尼古丁依赖和转吸香烟相关，医生呼吁政府加强监管限制。

structure.summary: 电子烟与呼吸症状、尼古丁依赖和随后吸烟明确相关
落实素色包装、移出视线、简化口味名，并限制口味数量
十年使用增十倍，长期影响未知，需跟上市场持续监管

hard.s: Vaping should not be seen as a harmless part of growing up, while concerns about wider impacts on young people's health continue to grow.
hard.t: 电子烟不应被视为成长过程中无害的一部分，而人们对电子烟影响年轻人健康的更广泛担忧也在增长。
hard.a: while 引导并列对比；be seen as 意为被视为；concerns about 意为对…的担忧。

title: Barking mad? How England's least friendly borough feels about the ranking
content: Alice Fokuo is so friendly with her neighbour that they have exchanged keys to each other's homes. The level of intimacy is such that I call her mum, because she cooks for me. So the market trader was surprised to learn that her borough, Barking and Dagenham, ranked the least friendly in England in a new study drawing on government data from the community life survey. It measures how often people chat to neighbours, feelings of loneliness and belonging, local pride, and levels of participation in civic life in England's 296 local authority areas. Everyone who passes says hello, children run to me and say grandma and hug me. It's amazing. I don't know about other people, because everyone is different, but to me they're nice. I'm very happy. I belong here. However, she worried that the once-bustling market was losing its role as a community space as younger people make more purchases online. She values its sociable atmosphere. Many people in Barking's town centre who spoke to the Guardian shared Fokuo's fondness for their neighbours, but expressed concerns about living in London's most indebted borough and the lack of well-cared public spaces for socialising. Adrian Stan, a 31-year-old cleaner, appreciated that there was a friendly spot where he could mingle with friends and other local people for free, but bemoaned that there weren't more seating options in the square, and the state of its upkeep. He wanted the council to do more to support rough sleepers in the borough, which has high rates of deprivation, poverty and homelessness. But he added that he found that people in the borough, which is one of the UK's most ethnically diverse, were open to new people. They really listen to what you're going through. Rana Meybeci, 33, worries about spending time in areas that are visibly dirty and strewn with litter. She also feels unsafe in Barking town centre, due to the level of antisocial behaviour, drug addiction and street drinking. Although she does not feel proud of Barking town centre, she is happy living in nearby Barking Riverside, a newly developed residential neighbourhood. We have a really good community here, she said. George Mathew, 69, is also a longstanding resident. All the people are quite friendly and mingle, and we update each other online. If you want any help, they are ready to help out. The development has faced criticism for its limited infrastructure and a dearth of amenities, from cafes to GP services.
translation: 爱丽丝·福库奥与邻居关系好到交换了彼此家门的钥匙。亲密程度到了这种地步：我叫她妈妈，因为她给我做饭。因此，当这位集市商贩得知她所在的巴金-达格纳姆区在一项新研究中被评为英格兰最不友好的地区时，她非常惊讶。该研究基于社区生活调查的政府数据，衡量英格兰296个地方行政区内居民与邻居聊天的频率、孤独感和归属感、地方自豪感以及公民生活参与度。每个路过的人都说你好，孩子们跑过来喊我奶奶并拥抱我。这太棒了。我不了解别人，因为每个人都不一样，但对我来说他们都很友善。我很幸福，我属于这里。然而，她担心曾经熙熙攘攘的集市正在失去社区空间的作用，因为年轻一代更多在网上购物。她珍视集市热闹的氛围。巴金市中心许多接受《卫报》采访的人都认同福库奥对邻居的好感，但表达了生活在伦敦负债最重的地区以及缺乏维护良好的社交公共空间的担忧。31岁的清洁工阿德里安·斯坦很高兴有一个可以免费与朋友和当地人交往的友好场所，但抱怨广场上座位太少、维护不佳。他希望市政会更多支持该地区（贫困率、贫穷和无家可归率高）的露宿者。但他补充说，他发现这个英国民族最多元化的地区之一的人们对新人很开放：他们真的倾听你的遭遇。33岁的拉娜·梅贝奇担心在明显肮脏、垃圾遍地的地区度过时光，并因反社会行为、吸毒成瘾和街头饮酒而对巴金市中心感到不安全。虽然她不为巴金市中心感到自豪，但她很乐意住在附近新开发的住宅区巴金河畔：我们这里有一个真正的好社区。69岁的乔治·马修是这里的长期居民：我住的地方非常平静安宁，所有人都很友善、乐于交往，我们在网上互相更新近况。
summary: 伦敦巴金-达格纳姆被评英格兰最不友好地区，但当地居民反驳称社区友善；公共空间匮乏与债务问题才是真困扰。

structure.summary: 邻里关系亲密的巴金被评为最不友好，居民惊讶
多数人称赞邻居友善，但担忧债务与公共空间
巴金河畔新社区氛围好，但基础设施与配套不足

hard.s: The level of intimacy is such that I call her mum, because she cooks for me.
hard.t: 亲密程度到了这种地步：我叫她妈妈，因为她给我做饭。
hard.a: such that 引导结果状语从句，意为到了…的程度；intimacy 意为亲密关系。

title: Rough sleepers wary of Burnham pledge: 'You mean he has said some words?'
content: As Andy Burnham set out his plan to end rough sleeping on Tuesday night, volunteers from homelessness charity Under One Sky were offering hot drinks, sandwiches, socks and soap to dozens of rough sleepers around Tottenham Court Road in central London. Among those sleeping on the streets, the prime minister's plan was met with widespread scepticism born from long familiarity with similar political declarations. You can never end rough sleeping. I think he is taking on a monumental task, said a former construction worker in his 50s. He was living in a hostel after struggling to find work over the past few years, and was reluctant to sign on for unemployment benefits. Burnham has committed himself to the target; if he doesn't fulfil it, there will be problems. I wouldn't have done that, he said. Many said it was hard to follow the news without regular internet access, but several were aware that Burnham had made a commitment to end rough sleeping when he came to power. He has made a pledge? You mean he has said some words? said one man in his 60s who has been sleeping intermittently in a tent in front of a furniture shop for several years. He was reluctant to say why he was homeless, only that he had previously owned a restaurant before losing his house. Burnham has likened his plan to the Everyone In scheme launched during the Covid pandemic, which housed thousands of rough sleepers, mainly in hotels, during lockdown. But many working in the homelessness sector said it will not be easy to recreate this feat. Adam Soliman, a deputy manager at St Mungo's, said while the scheme was successful at getting people through the door, it did not help them to stop rough sleeping in the long term, largely because there were no permanent homes for people to move to. Bringing people in is great and gives them a sense of safety, but if there's no move-on options, we're just putting a plaster on the issue. Is there going to be more affordable housing for people? Is there going to be more money for mental health services? It's great to get everyone in by Christmas, but on 1 January, what's the plan? Lesley Howard, head of homelessness at a charity that helps substance misusers, said the answer would not be found by throwing more money at the issue. We need to think it through and we need to make sure there's longer-term funding because these things take time. A man who had recently been released from prison remained sceptical about whether Burnham would succeed. He says he is going to eradicate homelessness. He is writing cheques at the moment, and this one might bounce.
translation: 周二晚，当安迪·伯纳姆公布其终结露宿街头的计划时，无家可归慈善机构 Under One Sky 的志愿者正在伦敦市中心托特纳姆法院路一带，为几十名露宿者提供热饮、三明治、袜子和肥皂。在露宿街头的人群中，首相的计划遭到广泛质疑——这种质疑源于对类似政治宣言的长期熟悉。你永远无法终结露宿。我认为他在接下一项艰巨的任务，一名不愿透露姓名的50多岁前建筑工人说。他过去几年找不到工作，目前住在收容所，不愿登记领取失业救济金。伯纳姆已把自己与这个目标捆绑；如果他做不到，会有麻烦。我不会这么做。许多人说，没有稳定的网络很难跟上新闻，但有几个人知道伯纳姆上台时承诺要终结露宿。他做出了承诺？你是说他说了几句话？一名60多岁、多年来间歇性睡在家具店前帐篷里的男子说。他不想说为什么无家可归，只说自己曾拥有一家餐馆，后来失去了房子。伯纳姆将他的计划比作新冠疫情期间推出的 Everyone In 计划，该计划在封锁期间为数千名露宿者（主要是在酒店）提供了住所。但许多无家可归领域的工作者表示，重现这一壮举并不容易。圣蒙戈慈善机构的副经理亚当·索利曼说，虽然该计划成功让人们进了门，但并未帮助他们长期停止露宿，主要是因为没有永久住房可搬。把人接进来很好，给了他们安全感，但如果没有后续安置选项，我们只是在伤口上贴创可贴。会有更多经济适用房吗？会有更多钱投入精神健康服务吗？让大家在圣诞节前住进来很好，但1月1日呢，计划是什么？一家帮助药物滥用者的慈善机构的负责人说，答案不是往问题上砸更多钱。我们需要想清楚，确保有长期资金，因为这些事情需要时间。一名刚出狱的男子对伯纳姆能否成功仍持怀疑态度。他说要消灭无家可归，他现在是在开支票，而这张支票可能会跳票。
summary: 首相伯纳姆承诺圣诞前终结露宿，但露宿者与慈善机构普遍怀疑：缺乏永久住房与后续安置，承诺恐成空话。

hard.s: Bringing people in is great and gives them a sense of safety, but if there's no move-on options, we're just putting a plaster on the issue.
hard.t: 把人接进来很好，给了他们安全感，但如果没有后续安置选项，我们只是在伤口上贴创可贴。
hard.a: 动名词 Bringing people in 作主语；move-on options 意为后续安置选择；put a plaster on 意为敷衍了事、贴创可贴（比喻治标不治本）。
